rationale: Plural noun in line 1 ⲥⲁⲩⲉ ⲛ̄ⲛⲣⲁⲓ̈ ⲉⲧⲥⲁⲍⲧ ⲁⲡⲛⲟⲩⲃ 'beauty of the X inscribed with gold.' Etymology uncertain; possibly a Lyc. lexeme for ornate luxury items (jewelry, vellums, embroidered fabrics). Fits parallel with garments-of-silk in line 1-3.

Compound or single noun spanning lines 1-2 ⲛ̄ⲛⲥⲍⲓ-|ⲁⲙⲉ. Possible parsing: ⲥⲍⲓ (= ⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ 'writing/embroidery') + ⲁⲙⲉ ('fine linen'). The 'garments of embroidered linen of silks' fits the luxury-textile inventory; parallel with ⲉⲧⲥⲁⲍⲧ 'inscribed/embroidered' in line 1.

Recurs at lines 5 and 13 in the structurally pivotal phrase ⲧⲇⲁⲙ ⲙ̄ⲡⲛⲟⲩⲥ ⲛ̄ⲟⲩⲁⲓⲛⲉ 'the taming of the Mind of Light.' Likely Greek δάμασις 'subjugation' or related to Coptic ⲧⲱⲙ 'bind, shut.' Manichaean technical term for the Light-Mind's subduing operation upon the body's passions.

In apposition to ⲧⲉⲡⲓⲑⲩⲙⲓⲁ at line 6: 'desire, the tyrant of the body.' Likely Lyc. nativized form of Greek τύραννος. Captures the despotic rule of desire over the body that the Mind of Light has now humbled.
Recurs lines 7, 15. Verb of motion away in negative-soteriological context: phantasies and evil mysteries flee before the new dispensation. Likely from ⲣ̄- + ⲡⲱⲧ/ⲡⲱⲱⲧⲉ 'flee, leap.'
Auditory-affective term in line 11 'the X of evil' parallel with 'the noise (ⲟⲩⲭⲗⲉ) of desire.' Possibly Greek πειθώ 'persuasion' or πάθος 'passion' with Lyc. orthographic adaptation. Confidence low.
Line 23 ⲉⲙⲛ ⲡⲉⲧⲍⲓⲭⲱϩ 'with no one set above (Sin)/no one to restrain it.' Probable parsing ⲡⲉⲧ-ϩⲓ-ϫⲱ-ϥ̄ 'the one upon him.' Captures the unchecked dominion of Sin in the pre-conversion body.
Greek loanword ὄχλος 'crowd, noise, disturbance' (or ὀχλή 'annoyance'). Line 11 'the noise of desire' as one of the vain auditory inputs that filled the ear before the Mind of Light's dominion.

Line 9 ⲛⲍⲃⲥⲁⲩⲉ ⲉⲧⲱⲏⲥ ⲣ̄ⲉⲛⲉϩ 'garments that abide forever.' Likely qualitative of a Lyc. enduring-verb related to ⲱⲥⲕ̄ 'tarry, prolong' or ⲱⲱϣ 'be wide, abundant.' Modifies the eternal garments of righteousness contrasted with the perishable luxury garments.
